subject: GPU commit lexicon + proposed remedy ladder for Dedicated pool — Sunridge Health
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Torres <alyssa.torres@sunridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU commit — proposal + definition checklist

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks for taking the call last week. Per our discussion I attached a short proposal that maps the commit levels we discussed (base, sustained, burst) to expected throughput in tokens/sec for the two workload profiles you shared (interactive chat, bulk embedding). The PDF has an example capacity calendar and billing illustration.

Two quick clarifications we want solidified in contract language before we proceed:
- Definition: "Capacity Unit" = 1 vGPU-hour of dedicated inference throughput pegged to the p95 config of the selected instance family. We included a table showing how that translates to tokens/sec by model class.
- Remedy ladder: we propose a 3-step service credit ladder tied to monthly availability of the committed pool (>=99.5%, 98.0-99.49%, <98.0%).

If you want us to convert the table into an attachable clause we can draft redlines for legal. Can you confirm procurement prefers credits as % of monthly committed fee vs. fixed-dollar credits?

Best,
Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Sunridge_Dedicated_Commit_Proposal_v1.pdf

From: Alyssa Torres <alyssa.torres@sunridgehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Cole <ben.cole@sunridgehealth.com>, procurement@sunridgehealth.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU commit — proposal + definition checklist

Thanks Stephanie —

Saw the proposal, looks sensible. A couple of asks from procurement before we move to legal:
1) We need exact wording for "Capacity Unit". Our billing team will only accept chargeable units that are deterministic. Can you provide a single-line definition we can copy into the SOW?
2) For throughput guarantees, can you map tokens/sec to our 95th/99th percentile latency targets for the interactive profile? We need the SLA to reference measurable metrics.
3) Regarding credits: preference is fixed-dollar credit applied against the monthly committed charge (reduces payment amount). Percentage credits create accounting friction for us.

Also, Ben asked whether burst capacity is billed separately or drawn from the committed pool — please clarify in your next note.

Cheers,
Alyssa
Alyssa Torres
Director, Procurement, Sunridge Health

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 08:48:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Dedicated GPU commit — procurement asks (Sunridge)

Folks — forwarding procurement's asks. Quick run: Marcus, can you confirm the tokens/sec to p95 latency mapping for the c-models in the attached CSV? Lauren, legal will want a short clause for the Capacity Unit definition and for the remedy ladder (fixed-dollar credits as requested).

I'm proposing we respond with: 1) a one-line "Chargeable Capacity Unit" definition, 2) a throughput-to-latency table (p95/p99) for both interactive and batch profiles, and 3) an explicit sentence stating "burst capacity up to 20% of committed throughput is billed at the burst rate and subject to availability" — that should cover their question.

If you agree I'll prepare Sunridge_Redlines_v2.docx with inline suggested language.

-Steph

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Dedicated GPU commit — procurement asks (Sunridge)

Steph —

Attached CSV has p95/p99 latency estimates across our common model families (c-base-8g, c-pro-16g, etc.) at the commit-backed continuous throughput point. A suggested single-line definition: 

"Chargeable Capacity Unit (CCU): one (1) hour of dedicated inference capacity measured at the instance configuration and model variant specified in the Order Form; chargeable hours are rounded to the nearest minute and billed against the Customer's monthly committed hours."

On burst: agreed with your 20% cap, but add: "Burst consumption beyond the committed pool will be billed at the published burst rate and will not trigger SLA credits." That prevents customers from triggering credits by over-consuming.

I'll add the numbers into the redline doc.

-Marcus
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: throughput-metric-table.csv

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Torres <alyssa.torres@sunridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Cole <ben.cole@sunridgehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 13:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU commit — proposal + definition checklist

Alyssa —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attached is Sunridge_Redlines_v2.docx with: 1) a concise Chargeable Capacity Unit (CCU) definition you can paste into the SOW, 2) a throughput-to-latency table that maps tokens/sec to p95/p99 latency buckets for the interactive profile, and 3) the proposed remedy ladder expressed as fixed-dollar credits against the monthly committed fee (your preference).

Key points in the redline:
- CCU definition (one-line) as drafted by Marcus.
- Remedy ladder: >=99.5% availability = no credit; 98.0-99.49% = $5,000 credit per percentage point below target (cumulative), <98.0% = $10,000 credit plus right to termination for material breach if sustained for two consecutive months.
- Burst policy: up to 20% of committed throughput allowed; consumption above that billed at published burst rates and explicitly excluded from SLA calculations.

Please review and flag anything you can't accept — if procurement wants a smaller fixed-credit step we can negotiate that (we've modeled economics in the attached CSV).

If this looks OK we'll send to your legal for formal redlining and to DocuSign for signature-ready attachments.

Best,
Steph

Attachments: Sunridge_Redlines_v2.docx, throughput-metric-table.csv

From: Ben Cole <ben.cole@sunridgehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Alyssa Torres <alyssa.torres@sunridgehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@sunridgehealth.com, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU commit — proposal + definition checklist

Team —

Reviewed the redlines with our finance/ops and procurement. Two quick asks before we route to legal: 1) Can you change the credit step to a flat $4,000 per 0.5% below target instead of the cumulative per-percentage approach? That gives more predictability. 2) We need the CCU rounding rule changed to "rounded down to the nearest minute" (we bill against committed hours and want to avoid accidental upward rounding).

If Redwood accepts those two items we can aim for legal review and a signature the week of Aug 3.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Cole
Sr. Manager, Cloud Operations, Sunridge Health
